mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen monotonically from -69.4% to -64.7% over four weeks, signaling gradual return to office routines. This trend will continue, driving weekday commute-adjacent retail visits and lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 4.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility declines in week t+1 or t+2, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 29.3% to 26.7% over four weeks, indicating residents are spending less time at home and more time outside. This behavioral shift will accelerate retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks, producing higher RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.6 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases in week t+1 or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility recovered from -27.7% in week t-2w to 5.7% in week t-1w, then declined to -3.6% in week t-0w. If PARKS mobility rebounds above zero in week t+1, it signals weather or policy-driven outdoor activity resumption that will substitute for indoor retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises above 0 in week t+1
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS volatility from -27.7% to 5.7% to -3.6% suggests sensitivity to external conditions
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains below -5% for all of weeks t+1 through t+4, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -76.4% to -73.0% over four weeks, indicating gradual public-transport reopening. When TRANSIT crosses -70% in week t+1, it signals sufficient mobility infrastructure recovery to enable retail foot traffic, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.4 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility remains below -70% through week t+4, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized at -29.3% for two consecutive weeks, indicating essential-goods shopping has reached a floor. Concurrent WORKPLACES recovery and RESIDENTIAL decline signal consumers are shifting discretionary spending from home-based to out-of-home activities. The interaction of stable essential mobility with rising workplace presence will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within ±2 percentage points of prior week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM unchanged from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility falls below -35% in week t+1, or WORKPLACES mobility declines, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility exhibits high volatility (-27.7% to 5.7% to -3.6%), suggesting weather or seasonal sensitivity. If PARKS mobility turns positive in week t+1 and TRANSIT mobility simultaneously exceeds -72%, outdoor recreation and public-transport availability will jointly suppress indoor retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered to 5.7% in week t-1w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains negative through week t+4, or TRANSIT mobility falls below -73%, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved 4.7 percentage points over four weeks while RETAIL_REC has improved only 2.6 percentage points, indicating workplace recovery is outpacing retail recovery. If WORKPLACES continues to improve at the current rate and crosses -60% in week t+2, retail will lag further as workers prioritize commuting over discretionary shopping, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility remains below -60% through week t+4, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean by more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -76.4% to -73.0% while RETAIL_REC has improved from -79.7% to -77.1%, showing retail is recovering faster than transit. This decoupling indicates retail is reopening independent of transit infrastructure. If TRANSIT remains below -72% through week t+1 while RETAIL_REC continues improving, it signals retail reopening is policy-driven rather than transit-dependent, sustaining RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -72% AND RETAIL_REC improves week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT exceeds -70% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC declines in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.
